WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender,
           COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
), gender_shares AS (
    SELECT gender,
           order_count,
           1.0 * order_count / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_counts
), shares_with_average AS (
    SELECT gender,
           order_count,
           share,
           AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share
    FROM gender_shares
)
SELECT gender,
       order_count,
       share,
       share - average_share AS share_minus_average
FROM shares_with_average
WHERE share > average_share;

assumptions.assumption: Genders represented by at least one qualifying order with an invoice are the genders included in the average; NULL gender, if present, is treated as its own group.
